stories.headline: Supreme Court Issues Notice To Centre On Pleas Challenging Mandate To Sing Six-Stanza Version Of Vande Mataram
stories.title: Supreme Court Issues Notice To Centre On Pleas Challenging Mandate To Sing Six-Stanza Version Of Vande Mataram
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today issued notice on two petitions challenging the Union Government's January 28 and July 9, 2026 orders prescribing a six-stanza version of 'Vande Mataram' for singing and playing on specified occasions.

One petition has been filed by BD Borkar, a Scheduled Caste Buddhist, Ambedkarite activist and former National President of the All India Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation (BAMCEF).
The other petition is filed by a former IAS officer from Kerala, Balakrishnan Sathyabhama Mavoji, who belongs to the Scheduled Caste community.
As soon as the matters were taken, the bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana issued notice to the Centre.
Dr G Mohan Gopal appeared for the petitioners.

"By imposing sectarian prayer to particular Goddesses of one particular religion as the National Song of India, the Impugned Orders convert the character of the polity of India from a 'secular republic' to a 'theocracy'," Borkar stated in the petition.

According to him, such an imposition will "irreversibly deepen communal division and conflict in India by outraging the religious and spiritual feelings of minority religions including the religion of the petitioner (Buddhism);" The move, it is contended, makes a "a mockery of the foundational Constitutional basic structure features of fraternity and secularism."

The petitioners contend that the Centre has effectively replaced the two-stanza version of 'Vande Mataram', which has traditionally been sung at national functions since Independence, with the six-stanza composition appearing in Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel Anandamath.
The petitioners argue that the two-stanza version, which predates the novel Anandamath, is distinct from the six-stanza composition incorporated into the novel in 1881.
According to the petition, the original two stanzas describe the natural beauty of the motherland, whereas the additional four stanzas invoke Hindu goddesses Durga, Lakshmi and Saraswati.
According to them, Anandamath is a novel "filled with violent and hateful invective against Muslims", and the six-stanza version of the song is used in the context of a war cry.
Leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Rabindranath Tagore had objected to the adoption of all six stanzas, and the first two stanzas were accepted as a formula put forth by Tagore.

stories.headline: Hyderabad jolted by mysterious boom and tremors, experts rule out major earthquake
stories.title: Hyderabad jolted by mysterious boom and tremors, experts rule out major earthquake
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A mysterious boom and brief ground vibrations sent residents rushing outdoors across several Hyderabad neighbourhoods, prompting scientists to explain the possible geological cause.

A deafening boom, trembling floors and terrified residents rushing out of their homes turned an otherwise ordinary Tuesday morning into a scene of panic across Hyderabad's south-western outskirts, after an unexplained burst of sound and ground vibrations rattled several residential neighbourhoods.
Residents across Rajendranagar, Upparpally, Attapur, Erraboda, Keshavswamy Nagar and Langar Houz reported the incident at around 10.25 am on October 27.
The vibrations reportedly lasted five to 10 seconds, rattling windows and shifting household utensils, leaving many people wondering whether an earthquake had struck the city.
As alarm spread across the affected localities, residents stepped out of their homes and gathered in open spaces, fearing that the tremors could signal a larger seismic event.
The sudden, explosion-like noise added to the confusion, prompting speculation about its origin.

However, scientists at the Hyderabad-based National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) moved to dispel reports of a major tectonic earthquake, pointing instead to a localised geological process known as hydro seismicity as a possible explanation for the phenomenon.
What caused the mysterious boom?
Experts say that Hyderabad's geological setting offers important clues to understanding the incident.
The city lies on a stable crystalline granite shield, making a destructive earthquake highly unlikely.
Nevertheless, localised micro-seismic activity can occur beneath the surface.
Water penetrating deep into the ground, particularly amid intense seasonal or persistent rainfall, can enter tiny pores and fractures in underground rock formations.

stories.title: Minister Tummala Nageshwara Rao cautions officials and people over cyclone Arnab
stories.summary: Telangana Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao urges officials and farmers in Khammam district to take precautions against Cyclone Arnab, protect crops, conserve irrigation water and ensure uninterrupted drinking water and power supply.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Telangana Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao urges officials and farmers in Khammam district to take precautions against Cyclone Arnab, protect crops, conserve irrigation water and ensure uninterrupted drinking water and power supply.
Agriculture and Marketing Minister Tummala Nageswara Rao asked officials to take precautions to tackle drinking water and irrigation supply issues in undivided Khammam district.
During a review meeting at Khammam Collectorate, he discussed ways to protect crops after cyclone, Irrigation water, drinking water and Electricity supply.
He urged officials of the Irrigation Department to create awareness in villages and ask farmers to grow other crops instead of paddy during upcoming Yasangi (rabi) season.
He also advised them to conserve water used from Seetharama Project canals and Nagarjuna Sagar Left Canal.
The official were asked to take suitable steps to close canal shutters.
Farmers were requested to protect their standing crops from the cyclone Arnab.
They were asked to constantly monitor the situation along with officials from the Department of Agriculture, Horticulture and Marketing.
Marketing officials should also help farmers get good market rates for crops and pre-plan to ensure smooth procurement.
Departments were requested to work together to ensure there are no shortages of drinking water and power due to El Niño.
There should be no negligence from officials regarding supply of drinking water to the public or essential services to farmers.
Preventative action should also be taken to avoid losses due to lack of irrigation water.

stories.title: Odisha’s contempt petition in Supreme Court over Kotia panchayat election | Explained
stories.summary: The Odisha government filed a contempt of court petition against the Andhra Pradesh government in the Supreme Court challenging the notification for the forthcoming election in Kotia
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'supreme court' in summary weight 26.4
article_sentences: The story so far: The Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission issued a notification on October 19, 2026, for elections to the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituencies (MPTCs) and Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituencies (ZPTCs), scheduled for November 3.

The decision to hold the elections in the Kotia group of villages, whose jurisdiction has been disputed by Andhra Pradesh and Odisha since Independence, triggered protests across the political spectrum in Odisha.
The Biju Janata Dal (BJD), Congress, and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused Andhra Pradesh of undermining Odisha’s territorial integrity.

The Odisha government said on October 23, 2026, that it had filed a contempt of court petition against the Andhra Pradesh government in the Supreme Court challenging the notification for the forthcoming election in Kotia.
Why Kotia is disputed?
As many as 21 villages in the Kotia group, under Pottangi Tahasil of Odisha’s Koraput district, have been at the centre of a territorial dispute with Andhra Pradesh since 1955.
According to an Odisha government brief on the dispute, Odisha exercised administrative control over these villages from 1936.
The dispute surfaced in 1955, two years after the formation of Andhra Province, when Andhra Pradesh officials attempted to collect land revenue from the villages.
Odisha protested through its Chief Secretary, but Andhra Pradesh countered that it had been collecting revenue there since 1947 and that residents had participated in the State’s 1954 elections.
In 1959, Andhra Pradesh cited a 1942 boundary demarcation by M. Gilby, Assistant Director of Survey, Madras Province, claiming it had been carried out with Odisha’s consent.
Odisha rejected the claim, arguing that Gilby had wrongly assumed his demarcation conformed to the Government of India (Constitution of Orissa) Order, 1936.
Both States held general elections in the disputed area in 1967.

stories.headline: China’s 60,000 MW Dam Near The Border: What It Means For India And The Brahmaputra
stories.title: China’s 60,000 MW Dam Near The Border: What It Means For India And The Brahmaputra
stories.summary: China’s massive hydropower project on the Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet has sharpened India’s concerns over the future of the Brahmaputra. India’s proposed 11,200-megawatt Siang Upper Multipurpose Project in Arunachal Pradesh is being considered as a strategic response — but it has triggered fierce resistance from indigenous communities who fear displacement, ecological damage and risks to their ancestral lands. As protests intensify, we examine China’s megadam, India’s water-security concerns, the proposed project’s storage capacity, earthquake and environmental risks, and the demands of the Adi communities. Can India prepare for potential upstream threats while protecting local livelihoods and securing genuine public consent?

stories.headline: BRICS Forum adopts joint declaration; condemns Pahalgam attack, seeks UNSC reforms
stories.title: BRICS Forum adopts joint declaration; condemns Pahalgam attack, seeks UNSC reforms
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 27: The two-day conclave of the BRICS Parliamentary Forum on Tuesday adopted a joint declaration strongly condemning the 2025 Pahalgam attack and all acts of terrorism as it pledged to combat the menace in all its forms and manifestations and also stressed on non-intervention in the internal affairs of any country. The joint declaration, announced by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, also condemned the imposition of unilateral economic and secondary sanctions saying such coercive measures have far reaching negative implications on human rights, including the right to development, health and food security of people. The BRICS Parliamentary Forum supported a comprehensive reform of the United Nations, including its Security Council, saying this reform should make it more just, equitable, democratic, representative, effective, and efficient, better reflecting contemporary realities and the needs of the international community. "We express strong condemnation of any acts of terrorism as criminal and unjustifiable, regardless of their motivation, whenever, wherever and by whomsoever committed. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir (in Pahalgam) on 22 April 2025, during which 26 people were killed and many more injured. "We reaffirm our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorists, terrorism financing and safe havens," the declaration read. The Forum said terrorism should not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilisation or ethnic group and that all those involved in terrorist activities and their support must be held accountable and brought to justice in accordance with relevant national and international law. "We urge to ensure zero tolerance for terrorism and reject double standards in countering terrorism. We emphasise the primary responsibility of States in combating terrorism and that global efforts to prevent and counter terrorist threats must fully comply with their obligations under international law, including the Charter of the UN...," it read. The Forum said it looks forward to further deepening counter-terrorism cooperation and calls for an expeditious finalisation and adoption of the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism in the UN framework and concerted actions against all UN-designated terrorists and terrorist entities. "We reaffirm our adherence to the principles of sovereign equality, mutual respect, non-intervention in internal affairs, and the peaceful settlement of international disputes, as enshrined in the United Nations Charter, as essential foundations for global stability, peace and development," it said. The Forum reaffirmed its unwavering support for the peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the two-state solution, with the two States living side by side, in peace and security, in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions. It asserted the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom, and an independent, sovereign State. The Forum expressed deep concern over the continued escalation of tensions in West Asia and, recalling the respective national positions, called for exercising maximum restraint, as well as avoiding actions that could further aggravate the situation. It strongly condemned all violations of international humanitarian law, including deliberate attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure, including in BRICS member states, as well as the denial or obstruction of humanitarian access and the targeting of humanitarian personnel. Iran and United Arab Emirates, which are directly involved with the West Asia conflict, are members of the BRICS. Apart from India, other member nations of the BRICS are: Brazil, Russia, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia and South Africa. The Forum underlined the need to address accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law. "We recognise international efforts undertaken by BRICS members to promote respect for, adherence to, and effective implementation of international humanitarian law," it said. Recognising the urgency of addressing climate change, the BRICS parliamentary body calls for intensifying efforts, through dialogue and international cooperation, to implement nationally determined contributions, strengthen mitigation and adaptation efforts, with a view to achieving the objectives of the UNFCCC and the goals of its Paris Agreement as applicable. The Forum acknowledge the transformative potential of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and information and communication technologies (ICTs). "We emphasise the necessity of ensuring the open, safe, secure, stable, equitably accessible, peaceful and interoperable use and development of ICTs environment while respecting sovereignty and national security of each country. "In addition, promoting energy efficiency of AI systems, fostering AI science and innovation, leveraging AI for economic growth and social good and mitigating potential risks would be essential for promoting a just, fair, equitable and prosperous future of all countries, especially those of Global South," it said.

stories.headline: Omar expands cabinet with 4 new ministers, triggers internal discontent and BJP criticism
stories.title: Omar expands cabinet with 4 new ministers, triggers internal discontent and BJP criticism
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 27: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah expanded his council of ministers on Tuesday with the induction of four new faces from the Kashmir valley, triggering internal party discontent and protests, even as the opposition BJP hit out at the ruling alliance over "regional and cultural imbalance". The four National Conference (NC) leaders, veteran politician Ali Mohammad Sagar, Mir Saifullah, Shameema Firdous, and Altaf Ahmad Wani (Kalloo), were administered the oath of office by Lt Governor Manoj Sinha at Lok Bhawan here. With all four inductees hailing from Kashmir, the expansion has shifted the balance of the cabinet in the two-year-old government heavily towards the valley. Seven ministers in the now 9-member council hail from Kashmir, while Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Chaudhary and Javaid Rana remain the only two representatives from the Jammu region. Independent MLA from Chhamb, Satish Sharma, was dropped from the cabinet to accommodate the new inductees. Ahead of the expansion, all ministers had formally submitted their resignations to the Chief Minister to facilitate the reshuffle. The maximum allowed strength of the JK council of ministers is nine, adhering to the statutory 10 per cent limit of the 90-member Assembly in the union territory. National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah said "a very good cabinet change has taken place. They (ministers) will work and try to ease the difficulties and problems of the people". The reshuffle sparked immediate anger among supporters of six-time NC MLA from Eidgah, Mubarak Gul, who staged a noisy protest outside the party headquarters at Nawa-e-Subah after his name was omitted from the cabinet list. Agitated workers raised slogans against the decision, calling it a grave injustice to a leader with 40 years of service. Before the swearing-in ceremony, Gul expressed his dismay to reporters, saying, "I will speak at an appropriate time. I have attended 20 oath ceremonies and every time I have been dropped. You can say I have been dropped again." In a swift bid to contain the mounting resentment, NC President Farooq Abdullah rushed to the party headquarters shortly after the ceremony and appointed Gul as the party's new general secretary, replacing Sagar, who joined the cabinet. "Party President Dr Farooq Abdullah sb today nominated senior party leader, MLA Idgah Mubarak Gul Sb as party's new General Secretary. Wishing Gul sb all the very best," NC spokesperson Imran Nabi Dar posted on X. Discontent was also voiced by another senior NC leader, Abdul Majid Bhat Larmi, who admitted feeling hurt at being left out but pledged loyalty to the party. "After all, we are human beings. The heart naturally feels hurt — there is no doubt about that. Here I am talking to you, but from inside, my heart is burning," an emotional Larmi said, adding that he accepted the leadership's decision. The expansion also drew sharp criticism from the BJP as the Leader of Opposition Sunil Sharma accused the Omar Abdullah-led government of creating a regional divide. "This is the first time that there is a regional and cultural imbalance," Sharma told reporters. "Governments have to take every community, region, and area along. Today, that was nowhere to be seen." Meanwhile, the Congress, an ally of the ruling coalition, opted to remain outside the government. JKPCC president Tariq Hamid Karra reaffirmed his party's stance, stating that the Congress will not join the council of ministers until statehood is fully restored to Jammu and Kashmir. Among the new inductees, Sagar — a seven-time MLA who took his oath in Urdu — has never lost an Assembly election since his debut in 1983. Saifullah, who won from Trehgam post-delimitation in 2024, alongside first-time ministers Wani (Pahalgam) and Firdous (Habbakadal), took their oath in English. Firdous, who also heads the NC's women’s wing, becomes the second woman minister in the cabinet alongside Sakina Itoo. The oath-taking ceremony was attended by Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather, senior alliance leaders, and opposition MLAs from both the BJP and PDP. Satish Sharma remained absent from the swearing-in ceremony.

article_sentences: Guwahati: The Chief Minister of Assam, Himanta Biswa Sarma has announced that the Assam Cabinet has approved a 12% horizontal reservation for eligible former Agniveers in specified posts across key state departments.

Sharing the update on social media, Sarma said the initiative aims to recognise the service and discipline of those who have served the nation and provide them with further employment opportunities in Assam.
The reservation will benefit ex-Agniveers who are domiciles of Assam and have completed their full four-year tenure under the Agnipath scheme.
As per the announcement, the reservation will apply to specified posts in the Assam.
Police, the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), the Forest Department, prisons, Home Guards, Fire and Emergency Services, and the Excise Department, among other designated services.
The state government has also indicated that annual recruitment drives for eligible candidates will begin in 2027.

Emphasising the importance of the decision, Sarma said the move was aimed at valuing the discipline and dedication of former Agniveers while creating new avenues for them to continue serving the state.

The initiative is expected to provide eligible former Agniveers with additional opportunities to join state government services after completing their military tenure, subject to the applicable recruitment rules and eligibility criteria.

stories.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response on news publishers' plea challenging data protection law
stories.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre's response on news publishers' plea challenging data protection law
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The plea seeks to strike down several provisions of the data protection law as unconstitutional.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued a notice to the Centre on a petition challenging various provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and its accompanying DPDP Rules, which allegedly infringe upon press freedom and the right to information.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the notice after hearing arguments from senior advocate Madhavi Divan, who appeared for the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA).
The court has listed the matter for further hearing on November 17, alongside other pending petitions.
It highlights that the absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activities could severely impede news reporting, weaken investigative journalism, and compromise source confidentiality.

During the proceedings, Divan described the petition as perhaps the first comprehensive challenge by what she termed the "legacy media", distinguishing traditional news organisations from citizen journalists.
"This is perhaps the first comprehensive petition by what we call legacy media.
There has been some debate over citizen journalists.
We are the traditional, conventional legacy media," she said.
The senior lawyer urged the bench to issue a notice on the application seeking an interim stay of the challenged provisions.

Divan argued that the law’s consent requirements could render routine news gathering and reporting unworkable, especially when journalists report on individuals who refuse to consent to the processing of their personal data.
"If I am left to the mercy of the data principal as to whether he or she will give consent, how will news be reported?" she asked.

stories.headline: Supreme Court defers hearing on pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, SIR decisions
stories.title: Supreme Court defers hearing on pleas against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, SIR decisions
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has deferred hearing petitions challenging CEC Gyanesh Kumar and Election Commission decisions linked to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court has deferred the hearing on petitions challenging decisions by Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission of India (ECI) related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
During the proceedings, the court granted petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh 10 days to file a rejoinder to the Election Commission's counter-affidavit.
The matter is likely to be taken up again on November 17, after the Diwali vacation.
The petitions raise concerns about the Chief Election Commissioner's functioning and decisions on the electoral roll revision exercise.
The SIR has become a major point of contention, with questions raised about the Election Commission's procedures and how it is conducting the revision process.
Responding to the allegations, the Election Commission maintained that the three disputed SIR-related orders, issued in June 2025, October 2025 and May 2026, were unanimous decisions.
The poll panel rejected the suggestion that Gyanesh Kumar had issued the orders unilaterally.
The Commission also said Form 6, which individuals use to apply for inclusion in electoral rolls, had not been amended.
The legal challenge comes amid continuing scrutiny of the SIR process and the Election Commission's decisions concerning electoral registration.
The revision exercise aims to update electoral rolls, but petitioners have objected to its implementation and the poll body's procedures.
With the hearing deferred, the Supreme Court is expected to consider the matter at a later sitting, subject to its schedule.
